title: Modern public health and sanitation
summary: England's Public Health Act of 1848 aimed mainly to help build water supplies and sewerage, and it set up local and central units of government responsible for health. In the United States, improved sanitation dramatically reduced typhoid and cholera, and public health accounts for about 25 years of the gain in lifespan since 1900. Worldwide, in 1800 no region had a life expectancy above 40 years. Global average life expectancy rose from 32 years in 1900 to 71 by 2021, through many advances in health.
